newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures finish lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures finish lower.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures finished lower as the market muddled through rumors about the European monetary union (EMU), traders and analysts said.
"The only clear thing is that the dollar is ending at the top of its range this week," George Tzanetatos, vice president at Merrill Lynch, said.

June marks held only slim gains due to Germany Finance Minister Theo Waigel's comments around midsession, floor traders said. Waigel said Germany's budget deficit will be three percent of gross domestic product, and that there was no talk in the government about delaying EMU.
Some currency futures traders said that a strict adherence to the January 1999 launch date would result in a weaker euro, and thus push marks lower.
June marks shot up to $0.5812, widening out the day's range, on rumors that the start of the EMU would be delayed.
Traders said such rumors helped spark rallies in both U.S. T-bonds and U.S. stocks.
As yields on the U.S. cash bond slumped, June yen strengthened. Some traders said expectations that the U.S.-Japan interest rate differential would narrow supported yen futures for most of the day.
June yen settled near the daily high at $0.008745. Resistance was seen at the 200-day moving average at $0.008753.
In addition, trade expert Fred Bergsten reportedly told another wire service that yen needs to be 10 percent stronger against the dollar, and sees dollar/yen fairly valued at 90 to 100 spot.
The 90 to 100 spot yen area corresponds to $0.011237 to $0.010126 in September yen.
September becomes lead contract month in all currency futures on Monday.
The last trading day for June is on Thursday, June 12.
Bergsten's comments also supported U.S. T-bonds, thus weighing on U.S. yields, some traders said.
Uncertainties about the fate of EMU, particularly ahead of the EU summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17, failed to support Swiss franc futures.
June Swiss francs found little flight-to-quality buying, as the Swiss central bank has made it clear in recent days that an appreciating Swiss franc would be a major policy problem.
Floor traders said trade in the Australian dollar futures pit was surprisingly active, as the contracts staged a recovery.

At the end of pit trade, June yen closed up $0.000072 at $0.008733, marks were up $0.0008 at $0.5795, Swiss francs lost $0.0024 at $0.6899, sterling fell $0.0012 at $1.6318, Canadian dollars were down $0.0035 at $0.7234, Australian dollars were up $0.0019 at $0.7626 and Mexican pesos were $0.000150 at $0.124650.
